title: Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk) is now open weight | Mistral
gist: Mistral released open weights for Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk), a 1-trillion-parameter multimodal MoE trained from scratch in Europe, claiming leadership among open-weight models in agentic coding and defensive cybersecurity after three more weeks of RL. Priced at $0.70/$2.10 per million input/output tokens under a modified MIT license that requires Model-as-a-Service operators to buy a commercial license, it is pitched as the foundation of European sovereign AI, with backing from Booz Allen, Cisco, CrowdStrike, Orange Cyberdefense, Microsoft Foundry and European banks.

insights.claim: Mistral says just three weeks of additional reinforcement learning after the public preview pushed Mistral Large 4 to the top of open-weight coding, and that RL gains continue to accelerate with no signs of saturation.
insights.speaker: Mistral Blog
insights.so_what: If RL scaling is not saturating, post-training compute (not pretraining) drives near-term capability gains; bullish for RL infrastructure demand.
insights.quote: Gains continue to accelerate, with no signs of saturation.
insights.locator: Since then, we've put that feedback

insights.claim: On Cognition's private FrontierCode 2.0 benchmark, which judges whether a repository maintainer would merge an agent's change, Mistral Large 4 scored 19.7%, ahead of DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (19.3%), GLM-5.3 (17.8%) and Kimi K3 (17.3%).
insights.speaker: Mistral Blog
insights.so_what: Open-weight coding scores are tightly clustered, so leadership is narrow and contestable among Chinese and European labs.
insights.quote: Mistral Large 4 leads with a score of 19.7%.
insights.locator: On Cognition's private FrontierCode 2.0

insights.claim: Mistral Large 4 scores 48% on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, effectively tied with the leading open-weight model GLM-5.3, while using 47% fewer tokens per task on average.
insights.speaker: Mistral Blog
insights.so_what: Token efficiency directly lowers cost per agentic task, an increasingly important competitive metric beyond raw scores.
insights.quote: using 47% fewer tokens per task on average.
insights.locator: On the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index

insights.claim: On Terminal-Bench 4.0, Mistral Large 4 improved 13 percentage points from preview to 41%, leading open-weight models while cutting output tokens by 30%.
insights.speaker: Mistral Blog
insights.so_what: Shows rapid post-preview RL iteration can materially move agentic benchmarks within weeks.
insights.quote: Mistral Large 4 improved by 13 percentage points to 41% compared to its public preview
insights.locator: The gains extend to terminal-based coding

insights.claim: In Surge Code's blind pairwise human-preference evaluations, Mistral Large 4 beat GLM-5.3, Kimi K3 and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash but lost to Claude Opus 5.5, which was preferred on 78% of prompts versus 22% for Mistral.
insights.speaker: Mistral Blog
insights.so_what: A sizable gap remains between the best open-weight model and the closed frontier (Anthropic) on human-judged coding quality.
insights.quote: ranking behind only Claude Opus 5.5 among the models evaluated.
insights.locator: Beyond benchmarks, Mistral Large 4's coding

insights.claim: Mistral Large 4 now offers three reasoning modes (Low, Medium, High default), with Low replacing the former 'None' mode, letting developers trade performance against inference cost.
insights.speaker: Mistral Blog
insights.so_what: Tunable reasoning effort is becoming a standard pricing lever; it makes per-task cost comparisons across vendors harder.
insights.locator: To give developers greater control

insights.claim: Mistral Large 4 scores 51% on the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index, which tests vulnerability discovery, reproduction and patching, and Mistral says it handles legitimate defensive tasks without unnecessary refusals.
insights.speaker: Mistral Blog
insights.so_what: Cyber defense is emerging as a premium vertical for open-weight models where enterprises need self-hosting.
insights.quote: Crucially, Mistral Large 4 handles these legitimate defensive security tasks without unnecessary refusals.
insights.locator: Mistral Large 4 scores 51% on the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index

insights.claim: Mistral reports that Mistral Large 4 refuses an average of 96.6% of malicious cyber requests across JailbreakBench, StrongREJECT and AgentHarm prompts, the highest it measured among open models.
insights.speaker: Mistral Blog
insights.so_what: Safety claims are self-measured; regulators and buyers will want third-party verification before relying on them.
insights.quote: achieving an average refusal rate of 96.6% on malicious cyber requests, the highest we measure among open models.
insights.locator: Safety has improved alongside capability

insights.claim: Mistral admits that monitoring of live preview traffic showed potential uplift for conducting real cyberattacks despite refusals of black-box attacks on live targets, and it is tightening guardrails over the coming months.
insights.speaker: Mistral Blog
insights.so_what: An open-weight lab acknowledging offensive uplift raises regulatory and reputational risk around releasing frontier cyber-capable weights.
insights.quote: we see a potential for uplift to conduct real attacks. We are modifying our guardrails accordingly
insights.locator: In the time since the preview

insights.claim: Mistral is giving vetted enterprise design partners such as Orange Cyberdefense preview access to a specialized Mistral Large 4 variant for penetration testing, vulnerability assessment and red-teaming, under contractual safeguards restricted to authorized systems.
insights.speaker: Mistral Blog
insights.so_what: A gated offensive-security tier is a potential high-margin revenue line separate from the open release.
insights.locator: We are also providing enterprise design partners

insights.claim: Booz Allen Hamilton testing found Mistral Large 4 matched other frontier cyber models on vulnerability-detection recall in source code security analysis with a compelling cost curve, and valued its data-sovereign deployment for strict data-residency clients.
insights.speaker: Brad Medairy, Booz Allen Hamilton
insights.so_what: US defense-adjacent contractors validating a European open model widens Mistral's government addressable market.
insights.quote: The model was able to match vulnerability detection recall rates against other frontier cyber models with a compelling cost curve.
insights.locator: Testing by Booz Allen demonstrated

insights.claim: Cloudflare's chief strategy officer argues that a defense an organization does not control is exposure, so open-weight models that defenders can audit and self-host are necessary when threats move at machine speed.
insights.speaker: Stephanie Cohen, Cloudflare
insights.so_what: Security vendors are framing open weights as a control requirement, supporting demand for self-hosted security AI.
insights.quote: Worse, a defense you don’t control isn’t defense—it’s exposure.
insights.locator: When threats move at machine speed

insights.claim: CrowdStrike's Chief AI officer argues that powerful AI models alone will not tip the cybersecurity balance; security expertise, real-world threat intelligence and rigorous testing are also required.
insights.speaker: Dr. Bartley Richardson, CrowdStrike
insights.so_what: Suggests incumbent security vendors' data and expertise moats persist even as models commoditize.
insights.quote: Powerful AI models alone won't tip the scales in cybersecurity.
insights.locator: Powerful AI models alone won't tip

insights.claim: ENISA, the EU cybersecurity agency, is testing Mistral Large 4 alongside closed and open models to identify vulnerabilities, audit code and analyse defensive logs.
insights.speaker: Laura Heuvinck, ENISA
insights.so_what: EU institutional evaluation could translate into public-sector procurement preference for European models.
insights.locator: ENISA is experimenting with closed and open

insights.claim: Zscaler has integrated its Security for AI offerings, delivered on its sovereign Zero Trust Exchange in Europe, with Mistral, and says many European enterprises are already adopting Mistral Large 4 as their sovereign model of choice.
insights.speaker: Dhawal Sharma, Zscaler
insights.so_what: Security-platform integrations create distribution for Mistral and AI-governance revenue for Zscaler in Europe.
insights.locator: As enterprises bring AI into production

insights.claim: Mistral positions Mistral Large 4, trained from scratch on European infrastructure with clear lineage, as the trusted foundation for sovereign AI and says it is defining the sovereign AI category.
insights.speaker: Mistral Blog
insights.so_what: Sovereignty framing gives Mistral a non-benchmark moat with European governments and regulated industries.
insights.quote: Mistral is defining the sovereign AI category and leading the open frontier.
insights.locator: Mistral Large 4 ranks as the best

insights.claim: Mistral argues sovereignty means organizations can inspect, customize and deploy the model on their own infrastructure and improve it without depending on Mistral serving it through an API.
insights.speaker: Mistral Blog
insights.so_what: Mistral monetizes via customization (Forge), tooling (Studio) and Applied AI services rather than pure API margin.
insights.quote: They can use and improve Mistral Large 4 without depending on Mistral to serve it through an API.
insights.locator: Built for Sovereignty.

insights.claim: European financial institutions including La Banque Postale, ABN AMRO, Belfius and Crédit Agricole publicly back Mistral Large 4, citing self-hosting on their own infrastructure as key to strategic autonomy.
insights.speaker: Mistral Blog
insights.so_what: European bank adoption signals a regulated-industry demand base for sovereign open models.
insights.locator: This major investment by Mistral AI

insights.claim: Rubrik says customers want open-weight and private model options to meet data residency, latency, cost and capability requirements, and that Mistral gives European governments a credible option that does not route data to other countries.
insights.speaker: Anneka Gupta, Rubrik
insights.so_what: Data-residency rules are a structural tailwind for European model providers versus US hyperscaler-only APIs.
insights.locator: Rubrik supports Mistral and the push

insights.claim: Mistral concedes sovereignty does not always require self-hosting, and Microsoft is the first cloud provider to offer Mistral Large 4, via Microsoft Foundry with private deployment options for Azure.
insights.speaker: Mistral Blog
insights.so_what: Microsoft hedges its model portfolio with Mistral, keeping hyperscalers in the sovereign-AI value chain.
insights.quote: Sovereignty does not always require self-hosting; sometimes it just requires deployments that meet your control requirements.
insights.locator: Sovereignty does not always require

insights.claim: Hugging Face's VP Product argues AI sovereignty is not about choosing which API to call but having the freedom to run, customize and build AI on your own terms.
insights.speaker: Jeff Boudier, Hugging Face
insights.so_what: Open-weight distribution platforms benefit as sovereignty arguments gain traction.
insights.quote: AI sovereignty isn't about choosing which API to call.
insights.locator: AI sovereignty isn't about choosing

insights.claim: Mistral Large 4 is priced at $0.70 per million input tokens, $0.07 per million cached input tokens and $2.10 per million output tokens.
insights.speaker: Mistral Blog
insights.so_what: Aggressive pricing with 90% cache discount pressures closed-model API margins for coding agents.
insights.quote: Mistral Large 4 is priced at $0.70 input / M, $0.07 cached input / M, and $2.10 output / M tokens.
insights.locator: Starting today, Mistral Large 4 is priced

insights.claim: Mistral Large 4 ships under the Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight license, a modified MIT license that is free for use, fine-tuning and commercialization except that Model-as-a-Service operators must obtain a separate commercial license.
insights.speaker: Mistral Blog
insights.so_what: The MaaS carve-out protects Mistral's API revenue from inference resellers while keeping enterprise adoption open.
insights.quote: businesses that operate a Model-as-a-Service offering must obtain a separate commercial license from Mistral before using the model commercially.
insights.locator: The model is available to use under

insights.claim: Mistral Large 4 is distributed through Mistral Studio, the Mistral API, OpenRouter, Hugging Face weights for vLLM or SGLang, and NVIDIA-hosted endpoints and an optimized NVIDIA NIM container.
insights.speaker: Mistral Blog
insights.so_what: Broad day-one distribution including NVIDIA's stack lowers adoption friction for self-hosters.
insights.locator: Start building with Le Chonk

insights.claim: Mistral describes Mistral Large 4 as an open-weight hybrid instruct-and-reasoning MoE with 1 trillion parameters, multimodal input and native fluency in 160+ languages, and says it will be the foundation for a new generation of specialized Mistral models.
insights.speaker: Mistral Blog
insights.so_what: Expect a pipeline of distilled, task-specific Mistral models derived from Large 4.
insights.quote: Mistral Large 4 will serve as the foundation for a new generation of specialized and optimized Mistral models.
insights.locator: What's Next

insights.claim: Mistral Large 4's FinWorkBench (Finch) score rose from 67.4% in preview to 73.3%, second among open models only to Kimi K3 at 77.3%, driven by improved spreadsheet creation and editing for finance and accounting.
insights.speaker: Mistral Blog
insights.so_what: Finance workflow automation is a key enterprise wedge, and Chinese open models still lead here.
insights.locator: Mistral Large 4 has continued improving

insights.claim: Mistral's RL pipeline lifted BrowseComp web-browsing performance from 75% at an SFT checkpoint to 84.5%, above GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash but below Kimi K3's 91.2%.
insights.speaker: Mistral Blog
insights.so_what: Quantifies RL's contribution over SFT for agentic browsing, roughly a 9.5-point gain.
insights.quote: Our RL pipeline enabled us to reach 84.5% on BrowseComp (starting from an SFT checkpoint that was achieving 75%).
insights.locator: Web browsing is a critical part

insights.claim: On the B3 Agent Security Benchmark, Mistral Large 4 resisted 97.1% of attacks such as system prompt exfiltration and code injection versus 93.3% in preview, which Mistral says lets anyone hosting it run a safe agent without extra tuning.
insights.speaker: Mistral Blog
insights.so_what: Built-in agent robustness reduces the need for third-party guardrail layers, though security vendors still integrate.
insights.quote: meaning anyone hosting the model can run a safe agent without additional tuning.
insights.locator: Agents deployed by an organization
